title: Public Matrix Selection v1
objective: Wire Sage-compatible matrix selection, deletion, swaps, setters, block mutation, and row insertion through storage-neutral plans and existing generated exact-resource or packed-prime operations

handoff.summary: Public Matrix selection, deletion, rectangular submatrices, swaps, row and column mutation, exact block mutation, and dense-ZZ row insertion now execute through one lazy storage-aware module. Exact matrices stay in generated FLINT resources and packed-prime matrices preserve uint64 or M4RI storage; common typed-Python plans provide Sage-compatible ordering, validation, and transactional staging. Every exact staging, combined-selection, and cross-ring conversion resource is closed deterministically on success and error, while caller-owned resources remain open. Full self set_block is a validated no-op, and insert_row consumes Sage's exact ncols prefix while ignoring surplus input. Focused native/dynamic tests instrument ownership, prohibit hidden exact full-matrix exports, and retain cross-domain performance and swap-scaling history.
risks: Row and column swaps currently construct one full replacement matrix, so their square-matrix cost is O(n^2); the benchmark now retains 128, 256, and 512 scaling data for every canonical domain.
next_steps: Integrate the lane and run the focused public matrix selection test after any concurrent Matrix.py conflict resolution.

After the polynomial structural FFI lane integrates, run Public Matrix In-place Swap v1: declare FLINT fmpz/fmpq row and column swaps, add source-transparent M4RI and packed-prime kernels, and ratchet the retained scaling benchmark from O(n^2) to O(n).
